Sample.evidence_source: The number of participants (N = 249) exceeded the minimum 5:1 participants-to-parameter ratio needed to confidently examine a model (Bentler, 1990). In this study, a total of 225 participants were needed as there were 45 parameters (25 variable-to-variable paths, 10 standard error paths to the model variables, five BMI-to-variable paths, and five BMI standard error paths) in Fig. 1. Our sample size also exceeded the N ">= 200 recommendation for complex models (Weston & Gore, 2006).

Correlation between body appreciation an.evidence_source: The text states: 'Because BMI was related to five model variables (i.e., restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety, depressive symptoms, body appreciation, and intuitive eating), we controlled for BMI in the model by partialing out BMI's contribution to these variables.' This indicates a relationship but does not provide a specific Pearson r correlation coefficient between Body Appreciation and BMI.

The section also reports the variance accounted for in several model variables, including body appreciation and intuitive eating.
